why: The number of marks grows along each row, and row 3 (2 dots, 4 dots) needs more dots than 4. Options 2 and 3 both have 5 dots, but option 2 arranges them in the same 2-2-1 pattern as the 5 triangles at the end of row 1. So option 2 is the answer.
trick: When two options have the same count, compare the arrangement with the other cells.
note: By a strict "add 2" rule row 3 would need 6 dots, which no option has; the book answer B (5 dots in a 2-2-1 pattern) is kept.
